title: DNA supercoiling modulates bZIP transcription factor–DNA interaction
authors: Rosanna Mattossovich; Rosa Merlo; Gioacchino Schifino; Annamaria Sandomenico; Mikael Widersten; Antonino Caliò; Judith Peters; Annalisa Pastore; Antonietta Parracino; Anna Valenti
one_liner_zh: 该文结合生化实验与多尺度分子模拟，揭示DNA超螺旋拓扑状态通过调控bZIP转录因子GCN4碱性区构象集合来重塑其DNA结合识别，直接聚焦TF-DNA互作机制且方法含粗粒化模拟，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: DNA topology is a key regulator of chromatin structure and transcription, yet its direct role in transcription factor recognition remains unclear. Here, we investigate how distinct DNA topological states modulate binding of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae bZIP transcription factor GCN4 using topologically defined plasmids. By combining, complementary biochemical approaches, including Bio-Layer Interferometry applied here for the first time to topology-dependent protein–DNA interactions, we show that DNA supercoiling directly reshapes GCN4–DNA recognition. Positively supercoiled DNA forms more stable and persistent complexes, whereas negatively supercoiled DNA retains greater conformational heterogeneity. To interpret these effects, we performed multiscale molecular simulations. Coarse-grained simulations of plasmids recapitulate the global topology-dependent trends observed experimentally, while matched minicircle models reproduce the same behaviour at the local scale. In strong agreement with experimental data, simulations reveal that DNA topology modulates the conformational ensemble of the GCN4 basic region. Overall, positively supercoiled DNA promotes a more ordered binding mode and localized protein distribution, whereas negatively supercoiled DNA supports increased structural plasticity. These findings identify DNA topology as an active determinant of transcription factor recognition and provide a multiscale framework linking global DNA mechanics to local protein–DNA interactions. abstract_zh: DNA拓扑结构是染色质结构和转录的关键调控因子，但其在转录因子识别中的直接作用仍不清楚。在此，我们利用拓扑定义的质粒，研究了不同的DNA拓扑状态如何调节酿酒酵母（Saccharomyces cerevisiae）bZIP转录因子GCN4的结合。通过结合互补的生物化学方法，包括首次应用于拓扑依赖性蛋白质-DNA相互作用的生物层干涉测量法（Bio-Layer Interferometry），我们表明DNA超螺旋直接重塑了GCN4-DNA识别。正超螺旋DNA形成更稳定和持久的复合物，而负超螺旋DNA则保留更大的构象异质性。为了解释这些效应，我们进行了多尺度分子模拟。质粒的粗粒化模拟重现了实验中观察到的全局拓扑依赖性趋势，而匹配的微环模型在局部尺度上再现了相同的行为。与实验数据高度一致，模拟揭示DNA拓扑调节GCN4碱性区域的构象系综。总体而言，正超螺旋DNA促进更有序的结合模式和局部化的蛋白质分布，而负超螺旋DNA支持增加的结构可塑性。这些发现将DNA拓扑结构确定为转录因子识别的主动决定因素，并提供了一个连接全局DNA力学与局部蛋白质-DNA相互作用的多尺度框架。图形摘要
